items.creator: Thomas Shotter Boys
items.alt: Thomas Shotter Boys lithograph showing the corner turret of the Hôtel de Sens above a busy Paris street in 1839.
items.caption: The building was already being framed as a picturesque remnant. This is an authored print, useful for architectural and street context but not a photographic record.
items.creditLine: Thomas Shotter Boys; Musée Carnavalet, CC0
items.changeNote: A corner turret and the old street remain recognizable, while later façade symmetry is not the subject of this angle.

items.creator: Pierre Emonts or Emonds
items.alt: Pierre Emonts photograph of the Hôtel de Sens street façade in 1869 with the Confiturerie de Saint James sign over the entrance.
items.caption: The Confiturerie de Saint James sign makes the building's commercial occupation explicit.
items.creditLine: Pierre Emonts or Emonds; Musée Carnavalet, CC0
items.changeNote: Commercial signage occupies the main portal, which later becomes a library entrance.

items.creator: Anonymous
items.alt: Anonymous painting from around 1880 showing the Hôtel de Sens entrance and turrets on a snowy Paris street.
items.caption: An anonymous painter recorded the façade in winter. The scene supplies atmosphere and broad spatial evidence, not survey-grade detail.
items.changeNote: The façade reads as a complete street front, but the painting cannot establish precise condition.

items.creator: Eugène Atget
items.alt: Eugène Atget photograph looking past a corner turret of the Hôtel de Sens into the adjoining street around 1898.
items.caption: Atget's angle shows how tightly the old house met its neighbors.
items.creditLine: Eugène Atget; Bibliothèque nationale de France, public domain
items.changeNote: Adjacent buildings nearly touch the turret; modern views give the monument more visual space.

items.creator: Agence Rol
items.alt: Agence Rol photograph of the Hôtel de Sens in 1911, with an adjoining market structure close to the left turret.
items.caption: The city bought the building in 1911. The photograph records the hemmed-in street setting at that moment.
items.creditLine: Agence Rol; Bibliothèque nationale de France, public domain
items.changeNote: The market structure and neighboring fabric constrict the front view.

items.creator: Agence Meurisse
items.alt: Agence Meurisse photograph of the dark, unrestored Hôtel de Sens street façade in 1920, with a market wall, advertisements, pedestrians, and a car.
items.caption: The market wall, shopfront, signs, car, and pedestrians match the photograph supplied for this feature.
items.creditLine: Agence Meurisse; Bibliothèque nationale de France, public domain
items.changeNote: The main silhouette persists, while the dark surface, altered openings, commerce, and crowded edges differ sharply from the present.

items.creator: Gustave Ferdinand Boberg
items.alt: Gustave Ferdinand Boberg drawing of old houses being demolished opposite the Hôtel de Sens in 1926.
items.caption: Boberg titled the drawing as demolitions opposite the Hôtel de Sens. It records the changing block, not restoration work on the building itself.
items.creditLine: Gustave Ferdinand Boberg; Musée Carnavalet, CC0
items.changeNote: The surrounding block is visibly being cleared before the documented restoration campaign begins.

items.creator: Anonymous
items.alt: Paired stereoscopic photographs of the Hôtel de Sens façade, marked 1928–29.
items.caption: The mount is marked 1928–29, the period when the long restoration began. It does not prove a specific construction operation.
items.changeNote: The dark façade remains legible at the threshold of the 1929–1961 campaign.

items.creator: Guilhem Vellut
items.alt: Guilhem Vellut photograph of the restored Hôtel de Sens street entrance and its two corner turrets in 2016.
items.caption: The restored street front serves as the after frame. Its camera position is close but not identical to the 1920 view.
items.changeNote: The pale masonry, repaired roof and windows, open street edge, and library use replace the commercial 1920 setting.

items.creator: Bobo Boom
items.alt: Bobo Boom photograph looking up at the restored Hôtel de Sens from an oblique street angle in 2017.
items.caption: A wider oblique view confirms the current street entrance and turret arrangement while making the effect of camera position explicit.
items.changeNote: The modern block surrounds a restored monument that is visually more exposed than it was in 1920.
